test_title: PYST 05: SSC MTS 2024 - General Awareness (Held On: 07 Oct, 2024 - Shift 3)
subject: gk
question: A person having stunted growth and discoloured hair is most probably suffering from ________________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Protein Deficiency**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Protein deficiency can lead to stunted growth in children as protein is essential for the development and repair of body tissues.
 
• Discoloured hair, particularly a reddish-orange tinge, is a common symptom of severe protein deficiency, commonly referred to as Kwashiorkor.
 
• Kwashiorkor is more prevalent in areas with limited access to protein-rich foods, such as certain regions in Africa, Central America, and South Asia.
 
• Other symptoms of protein deficiency may include muscle wasting, edema, and an enlarged abdomen.
 
• A diet rich in legumes, nuts, dairy products, meat, and fish can help prevent protein deficiency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kwashiorkor**:

 
 
• A severe form of malnutrition caused by an inadequate intake of protein.
 
• Common in children in developing countries where diets are high in carbohydrates but low in protein.
 
• Symptoms include edema, irritability, ulcerating dermatoses, and an enlarged liver.
 
 
 
• **Marasmus**:
 
 
• Another form of severe malnutrition caused by an overall lack of calories and protein.
 
• Characterized by severe wasting of body fat and muscle, leading to a "skin and bones" appearance.
 
• Common among children in regions with food scarcity.
 
 
 
• **Essential Amino Acids**:
 
 
• Amino acids that the body cannot synthesize on its own and must be obtained from the diet.
 
• There are nine essential amino acids: histidine, isoleucine, leucine, lysine, methionine, phenylalanine, threonine, tryptophan, and valine.
 
• They are crucial for protein synthesis and other metabolic processes.
 
 
 
• **Protein-Rich Foods**:
 
 
• Foods high in protein include meat, fish, eggs, dairy products, legumes, nuts, and seeds.
 
• Incorporating a variety of these foods can help ensure adequate protein intake.
 
• Plant-based proteins can be combined to provide all essential amino acids, such as rice and beans.
